title: Android, Android TV, and Fire TV: Screen and controls
lead: Choose a source, edit separate source/player drafts and compare applied code, SDK state and events. This app also declares a TV launcher for Android TV and Android-based Fire TV; Vega OS is covered separately.

items.label: Implementation guide: PlayerConfig, source settings, UI customization and FAQ

blocks.text: Preparation and build

Build and launch apps/android using Android Studio or the documented command-line setup. Java 17 and required Android SDK packages are listed in Local setup and licenses and the implementation guide. The app uses Player 3.171.0. Allow com.playerlab.android on the Player license used by the build.

The same app declares a TV launcher for Android TV and Android-based Fire TV. Vega OS uses a separate app. The screenshots below were captured in a phone emulator; they do not establish remote-control reachability or playback on every TV or physical device.
Suggested screen workflow

Source and Theme selectors sit beside the playback preview. Settings, APIs, Code and More stay visible as workspace tabs, so opening an editor does not require scrolling through other panels. Settings groups configuration fields by purpose; APIs contains SDK operations, state and events; Code displays applied configuration; More contains additional tools and diagnostics.

items: Select VOD HLS or VOD DASH under Source and start playback. Confirm that the picture and position advance before changing settings.

Choose Settings → Configuration → Source, then Setting → Title. Keep the URL, enter Player Lab VOD and choose Apply source. Check the reload message and applied title without changing player settings.

Choose Player in Settings → Configuration. Use Setting to edit Startup buffer, Restart buffer and Forward buffer to 1, 2 and 10 seconds. Choose Apply player. Check the restart message, retained source and applied BufferConfig, then start playback if Autoplay is off.
Use Theme to compare Default, Sports, Live and Cinema. Android replaces PlayerView while keeping the Player. The player’s own menu is independent of the app settings workspace.

Use the Source or Player setting selector for audio, subtitles and bitrate with a source that provides suitable tracks or quality variants. A configured value does not add a missing track or rendition.
Choose Code to compare the applied settings. Use APIs → Commands, State and Events to connect an operation with its result.

For live rewind, load a live preset and wait for a seekable window. Live edge returns to the moving edge. More contains additional live controls and diagnostics; these are separate from the VOD settings.
If PlayerError or SourceError appears, note its numeric code. Check the allowed app identifier and source connectivity before treating the failure as a configuration issue.

blocks.text: Changing UI replaces PlayerView while retaining the Player and source. Return to Default after comparison. The custom modes need the bundled shared JavaScript/CSS; if absent, follow the implementation guide to build and synchronize them. In the recorded SDK 3.171.0 phone-emulator check, foregrounding kept playback paused; press Play to resume when needed.

blocks.title: Checking TV devices
blocks.text: The Manifest declares LEANBACK_LAUNCHER for Android TV and Fire TV. Focus navigation, button reachability, remote controls, and actual playback still need testing on each device. A successful phone-emulator test does not establish behavior on physical devices or TVs.
Configuration drafts and applying changes

In Settings, choose Configuration → Source, Player or SDK overrides, then the required Setting. Source and Player have separate drafts. The fixed action area reports unapplied changes and whether Apply reloads the source or recreates the Player. Applying Player settings uses the applied source, not unapplied Source edits. A validation failure keeps the draft and opens the affected field.

In Settings, choose the source group and the field you want to edit. Source fields are a custom HTTP/HTTPS URL, DASH/HLS/Smooth/Progressive type, optional title, optional poster URL, persistent poster, start offset in seconds, SDK-default/Start/End reference, and optional live target latency in seconds. Blank title, poster, and offset use SDK defaults. The default reference is the start for VOD and the end for live streams; the SDK corrects offsets outside stream boundaries. HTTP depends on the device network policy.

blocks.caption: Settings with Source selected. Choose a field from Setting; its editor appears above the fixed Reset draft and Apply source actions. Android 16 emulator.

blocks.text: Live target latency maps to SourceLiveConfig.targetLatency. Blank keeps the original SDK defaults (liveConfig = null). An explicit finite value changes the SDK’s definition of the live edge and asks it to approach that latency while avoiding stalls; VOD ignores it. Apply source reloads the source, player recreation retains the applied value, and Reset draft restores it without applying. This setting alone does not guarantee a seek-completion or latency-convergence deadline; the test results describe the checked environments.

Player fields are Autoplay (off), Start muted (off), SDK live time shifting (on), startup threshold (2.5 s), restart threshold (5 s), forward buffer (50 s), maximum automatic video bitrate (whole bps; blank means Int.MAX_VALUE / 2147483647, no ABR cap), preload (on), rebuffering (on), and live quality/stability balance (0–1; default 0.5). Thresholds must be nonnegative and at most forward buffer minus 0.5 s; forward buffer must be at least 0.5 s. Numeric fields reject non-finite values. The bitrate cap affects automatic selection; higher qualities remain available for manual selection. Balance applies near the live edge only. Player → Live time shifting is the SDK creation setting. More → Playback options → Enable live rewind controls is a separate app preference, available even while viewing VOD. It does not change VOD playback. More → Live controls shows current live actions only when the loaded source supports them.

blocks.caption: The Autoplay field in Player settings. Apply player recreates the player and reloads its source. Other player settings use the same field selector.

items: Choose Source in Settings → Configuration, edit the required Setting and use Apply source to reload it on the existing Player. Invalid drafts leave the applied source and Player unchanged.

Choose Player in Settings → Configuration and use Apply player for playback, buffer or adaptation changes. It creates a new Player with the applied source and its metadata/options, retaining UI mode, app rewind preference and the event log. Playback restarts according to the source start offset and Autoplay.

Reset draft restores the applied values for the selected Source or Player group. It does not apply defaults or restart playback. Changing the setting or workspace tab retains unapplied edits. Selecting a source preset replaces custom source fields and options.

blocks.text: Choose a group and a field to open its editor directly. Reset, Apply and draft status remain outside the field content. Source and Theme use selectors that show their available choices; a selected item has an explicit selection indicator. A disabled action has a separate unavailable state. Long structured inputs can scroll within their editor without moving the playback preview or workspace navigation.

Code displays Kotlin PlayerConfig, SourceConfig and PlayerViewConfig for the applied settings and current UI, including optional live target latency. Draft edits are excluded. Wrap lines controls line wrapping; Copy code writes the text to the Android clipboard and shows Copied. License keys use placeholders. The example still needs the integrating app’s keys, view attachment and lifecycle forwarding.

blocks.title: Menus inside the Android player
blocks.text: The player has its own settings menu inside the video. Scroll within that menu when an option is below its viewport. App settings are selected separately in Settings. PlayerTouchHost keeps a gesture that begins in the player with that view until it ends or is cancelled; replacing the player releases that touch ownership.

rows: Start offset: 5 seconds; Offset reference: Start
Apply source. On VOD, compare the first playback position with the beginning. Blank offset uses the SDK default. A retained offset also applies after a later player restart.
Apply player. Check that playback waits for Play and starts muted. These are startup settings, separate from immediate controls in the player UI.
Startup threshold: 1; Restart threshold: 2; Forward buffer: 10, all in seconds

Apply player. Startup/restart thresholds describe required buffered media before starting or resuming after a stall, not promised wall-clock delays. Inspect BufferConfig in applied code; the current network and source determine the visible effect.

Apply player. Inspect maxSelectableVideoBitrate in applied code and compare automatic quality on a multi-bitrate source. This caps automatic selection; higher qualities remain available for manual selection.

Apply player. Values toward 1 favor stability and values toward 0 favor quality near the live edge. VOD is unsuitable for comparing this setting. Preload content and Allow rebuffering are separate adaptation switches.
Player: en, de; Source: de, en

Apply the player list with restart, then the source list with reload. On a source containing those languages, check the selected audio in the player menu. The source list takes precedence; clear it to inherit the player list.
Apply player. Check the normalized retry list in applied code. A successful playback request cannot demonstrate retries; use a test source you control when investigating failure handling.

blocks.text: Reset draft abandons unapplied edits and restores the selected group’s applied values. To compare an SDK default, enter that field’s documented default and Apply; Reset is not a restore-defaults command. Select a source preset to clear custom source settings, including external subtitle metadata; player settings remain. Valid unchanged values can be applied again to explicitly reload the source or recreate the Player.

items: After Apply, choose Code → Player, source and UI and compare PlayerConfig, SourceConfig and the current UI configuration. Use Wrap lines to read long lines within the available width. Copy code writes the displayed text to the Android clipboard and changes the button to Copied.

Edit a draft without applying and check that the output stays unchanged. Actual license values are placeholders. Choose SDK overrides in the Applied code selector for the separately applied additional settings.

blocks.caption: Applied Kotlin configuration in Code. Wrap lines keeps long statements within the view. The export excludes draft edits and replaces the license with YOUR_PLAYER_KEY.

blocks.title: Reset is not Apply
blocks.text: Reset draft restores the selected group’s applied values without changing playback. Source and Player drafts remain separate. Separately applied SDK overrides remain active until removed and applied in the additional settings editor. Applying valid unchanged basic values deliberately repeats the selected reload or restart; check the action label before submitting.
Audio language, external subtitles and retries

Player audio language priority sets an ordered list such as de, en when the player is created. Source audio language priority overrides it for that source when nonempty; blank inherits the player list. Codes keep their priority after trimming and removing duplicates without regard to case. No match leaves the SDK default track.

WebVTT is a text-based subtitle format with timed cues. To add one external track, enter its HTTP or HTTPS WebVTT URL and optionally a label and language code such as en-US. Default external subtitle sets isDefault metadata; it does not enable the subtitles. Apply source, then select the track in the Default UI settings menu. Clearing the URL also requires clearing its metadata. Existing in-stream subtitles remain available.

HTTP retry delays (s) controls the wait before each retry. Blank uses the SDK policy that increases the wait between retries, none disables retries, and a comma-separated list such as 0, 0.25, 2 permits one retry for each finite nonnegative value. The setting applies after player recreation. This standard field does not edit callbacks, request credentials or content-protection license renewal retries; use the separate SDK settings for their supported inputs.

Source changes reload the current player; player language and retry changes recreate it. Both paths keep the applied source metadata, selected UI and app rewind preference. Reset changes the draft only. Code contains the same normalized settings and excludes unapplied text and actual license values.

items: To compare audio priority, apply Player en, de with restart, then Source de, en with reload. Read the selected audio in the player menu. Clear the source list and reload to inherit the player list.
To remove the external subtitle, clear its URL and metadata together and Apply source, or select a catalog preset. The Default external subtitle flag is metadata and does not enable captions.
To restore the normal HTTP retry policy, clear HTTP retry delays and Apply player. A successful request cannot demonstrate retry timing; compare failed requests only on a source you control.

blocks.text: Additional SDK settings

items: Choose Settings → Configuration → SDK overrides. Select a Feature, then use SDK setting to open one property. Search in the selector or browse its category; the editor appears without passing every matching field. Read the SDK name, type, accepted values and units.

Enter a value and choose Stage override. Check the staged changes, then Apply SDK. Staging alone does not affect playback; an applied override takes precedence over the basic settings. For scripts and lists with presets, Preset values inserts an example into the editable field; you can change it before staging.

Choose Code → SDK overrides and refresh the matching API State. Remove followed by Apply restores the basic value or SDK default. Reset draft discards staged edits and restores the applied overrides; it does not remove an active override.

For a callback such as LabelingConfig.videoQualityLabeler, read input and the required result, stage a body and Apply. Trigger the matching SDK path, then use More → Diagnostics to refresh callback outcomes and read calls, fallback and the last fallback reason.

rows: Choose the collection’s Edit button, then use Item and Property to edit one child field. Close editor retains the draft. Stage the entire list and Apply SDK. Subtitle default metadata does not enable captions; playlist preloading may increase network and memory use.
Companion ad container, SimpleCache or Cronet engine
These controls create real Android objects. Prepare the Google Play services Cronet provider before applying Cronet. The cache tweak reads existing cached media; ordinary playback does not fill it.
Enter a JavaScript function body using input. The field explains the return type. Stage and Apply before it runs. Inspect callback counts and fallback results afterward.

In More → Startup and integrations, save the setting, fully stop the app and reopen it. The current process value and saved next-launch value are shown separately. Debug logs can contain confidential information; keep them local.

blocks.caption: Recorded with the earlier app layout. An applied video-quality label callback. The staged body and active override are visible; the disabled Apply button indicates no pending change.

blocks.title: Callback execution
blocks.text: Callbacks use bounded plain values without Java/Android/Player object access. Invalid results or execution limits use the documented fallback. A zero call count means the SDK has not invoked that path. Read the implementation guide for language support, detailed limits and code reuse.
SDK operations, state and events

APIs separates Commands, State and Events. Select a category or search for an API, then choose the exact operation before running it. Search filters candidates; it does not execute a command. A command can submit asynchronous work, so its submission message is separate from the resulting SDK state and events. Keep a VOD source loaded for this seek comparison.

items: Open Commands, search Player.seek, enter 5 for time and Run API. Read any argument or source-state error.

blocks.caption: Commands with api.Player.pause() selected. Run API stays at the bottom. The call result and the observed SDK playback state are displayed separately.

items: Choose State, search Player.currentTime and Refresh SDK state. Read the value after seek completion; during playback it continues advancing. Refresh again after another command.

blocks.caption: State with Player.isPaused selected. Refresh SDK state reads the selected value once.

items: Choose Events and enable Record SDK events. Clear event counts before the next trial, perform Play/Pause or a supported seek, and inspect occurrence counts and latest SDK timestamps.

Zero means no occurrence has been recorded. PlayerView UI events use a separate prefix; playback belongs to Player and source events to Source. Clear event counts clears the history, not SDK playback state.

blocks.caption: Events with PlayerEvent.Paused selected. The selected event count and recent SDK event history are shown separately.

blocks.text: View commands install fullscreen, Picture-in-Picture and custom Web UI message handlers. Check availability before entering PiP, then inspect its actual view state. Fullscreen returns with Back without discarding editor drafts. Use the matching exit/disable action when finishing a host-feature comparison.

MediaSession connects the current player to Android media controls. Enable the native MediaSession command, inspect the controls, then disable/release it when finished. External-device behavior depends on the host system.

blocks.caption: Recorded with the earlier app layout. The native MediaSession command. Enabling it connects the current player to Android media controls; external-device behavior depends on the host system.

blocks.text: Cast, advertising, encrypted media and VR need matching content, a receiver/device or a connected service. Read availability and active state rather than the submission message alone. The VR renderer uses a real decoding surface and requires a compatible source VR content type; disable the renderer to restore normal PlayerView presentation.

Open More → Analytics and use the Analytics selector to choose collection settings, metadata or runtime actions. Apply Analytics recreates the player and reloads its source with the collection draft; Reset draft restores the applied settings. Perform a known playback and inspect collected sessions in Bitmovin Dashboard. A local SDK result does not prove backend receipt; the implementation guide explains Analytics/Observability after player integration.
Offline downloads and playback

items: Open More → Offline and choose Manager in the Offline selector. Choose Use sample DASH source or apply a downloadable on-demand source. Set Stable content ID, then Create manager. Keep the ID to address the same asset again.

Choose Download settings in the Offline selector, then use Setting to edit download/segment limits, device/network requirements and offline DRM handling. Choose Apply offline settings. Downloads can wait until all selected requirements hold.

Choose Actions → Fetch SDK track options. Then choose Track selection, select each required track and set Download, Delete or None. Process selected actions submits all selected track actions. Nothing is selected automatically; the SDK can reject an action that does not match the track state.

blocks.caption: Recorded with the earlier app layout. Selecting an audio track for download. This figure shows the selection step, before completion is established.

items: Inspect Progress and choose Actions → Read offline SDK state, then wait for the manager’s completed state. Only then choose Actions → Play downloaded source and compare video/audio with networking disabled. Track selection or submission is not completion.

In Actions, Suspend downloads and Resume downloads control work in progress. Delete all content for this ID removes its cached content; Release manager keeps the files while releasing the manager. Select a source preset to return to a remote source.

blocks.text: Offline DRM needs suitable rights, a license service and storage. License download/renew/release is separate from media-download completion. Advanced offline source constructor does not import an SDK-managed download or issue a license. For ordinary managed downloads use Play downloaded source so the SDK supplies matching cache/track metadata.
